cards.p: Architecture, materials, light, and atmosphere define the direction; a warm interior can lead to softer textures, muted tones, and calmer silhouettes.
Each function is mapped against movement, pace, and tools; reception, service, and clinical roles need different fits, pockets, and visual presence.
Fit, silhouette, and product categories are aligned into one wardrobe system, from shirts and aprons to overshirts, trousers, and outer layers.
Construction is chosen for the real routine: frequent washing, long shifts, easy replacement, and consistent repeat orders over time.

personalised.intro: The following sections show how we manage customisation in a structured way, from fabric selection to the definition of technical and production details.

accordions.p: Fabric selection is defined according to shift duration, climate conditions, level of movement, and maintenance requirements.
items: Examples: cotton blends, linen blends, easy-care technical fabrics
Main criteria: comfort, durability, visual quality, and stability over time and through washing

accordions.p: The colour direction begins with the space and the brand identity, then is validated under real operational conditions.
items: Examples: The colour range varies depending on the selected fabric, with the possibility of dedicated colour developments for larger-scale projects
Main criteria: consistency across roles and performance under different lighting conditions

accordions.p: Finishes define the identity of the garment while maintaining strong performance in daily use.
items: Examples: custom buttons, zips, labels, contrast topstitching
Main criteria: durability, ease of replacement, and visual consistency

accordions.p: Branding is developed according to the garment, frequency of use, and required level of visibility.
items: Examples: embroidery, tone-on-tone embroidery, woven labels, screen printing
Main criteria: durability, legibility, and carefully judged placement

cards.p: Local sampling and fittings allow for faster, more precise, and better-informed technical decisions.
Every garment is developed with movement, shift duration, and daily operational rhythm in mind.
Patterns, finishes, and specifications are archived to ensure consistent repeat orders over time, supporting team evolution.

faq.h2: Clear answers, before we even begin
faq.intro: Essential answers to the most frequent questions from hospitality, healthcare, and service teams.

items.q: Do you work from a catalogue?
items.a: No. Every project is shaped around your operational context, brand identity, and team structure. We can integrate existing bases when they offer a real advantage in terms of timing and cost, while still ensuring a final outcome that is custom, coherent, and distinctive.

items.q: Do you handle repeat orders after the first production?
items.a: Yes. Patterns, fabrics, finishes, and customisation systems are archived to ensure continuity over time. This reduces redevelopment phases, ensures consistency for new team members, and simplifies future repeat orders.

items.q: Do we need to start with a full wardrobe?
items.a: No. It is also possible to start with a single garment category or one specific role, and then expand the project over time. We define the most effective starting point together based on priorities, budget, and operational impact.

items.q: Do you develop colours and custom details?
items.a: Yes. We can work with existing colour cards to optimise lead times, or develop dedicated shades and finishes when volumes allow. Customisation techniques are selected according to durability, legibility, and garment type.

service-custom.v: FULLY CUSTOM UNIFORMS FOR YOUR TEAM
Professional wardrobes designed around your space, your team, and your operations
Every project starts from a blank page.
We do not adapt existing products. We develop garments designed specifically for your space, your team structure, and the daily reality of your service.
Uniforms are conceived as a coherent wardrobe system, not as isolated pieces.
Each garment works in relation to the others, ensuring visual harmony and operational functionality across the team.
What defines a fully bespoke project
Design that starts from the space
Architecture, materials, light, and brand atmosphere guide the visual direction of the wardrobe.
Each function is analysed in detail, reception, service, management, operations, to create garments aligned with movement, responsibilities, and work rhythm.
Fit, proportions, and lengths are defined to feel natural in the environment and ensure comfort during long shifts.

sector-hotels.v: Uniform systems for complex teams and layered environments

Hospitality settings bring together different departments, each with distinct functions and guest-facing contexts. Uniforms need to reflect the identity of the property while ensuring practicality, continuity, and operational reliability.

v: Alignment with architecture and brand identity

sector-restaurants.v: Food and beverage teams work in high-intensity settings. Garments must support the rhythm of service while balancing durability, comfort, and visual presence.

sector-wellness.v: In wellness settings, uniforms help create an atmosphere of calm and trust. The design prioritises softness, simplicity, and visual coherence with the identity of the space.

sector-medical.v: These garments support long working hours while maintaining an orderly, clean, and reassuring image. The approach prioritises functionality without giving up a refined aesthetic.

sector-service.v: Staff working in maintenance, logistics, and support need uniforms that are solid, functional, and consistent with the brand identity.

sector-guest.v: The team is the first tangible expression of the brand. Uniforms need to communicate professionalism and elegance while ensuring comfort in daily interaction.

phase-1.v: Understanding the context, defining the direction
Every project begins with an in-depth analysis of the context in which the uniforms will be used.
Space, operational flows, team structure, and brand identity guide the first decisions and define a clear direction for the entire wardrobe.
Reading the space and visual identity
The goal is to build a strong, shared foundation before development begins.

phase-2.v: The development phase translates the design direction into actual garments.
Fabrics, patterns, and construction are defined and tested through prototypes and fitting sessions to ensure comfort, functionality, and visual consistency.
Every decision is tested under real conditions of use to ensure long-term reliability.

phase-3.v: Once approved, the garments move into production with finalised patterns, materials, and finishes.
Local production allows direct quality control and greater reliability on delivery timelines.

parameter-quantities.v: A balance between quality and production sustainability. Minimum quantities vary according to garment construction and selected materials.
Woven garments: starting from around 10–15 pieces per style, distributed across sizes and variants
Knitwear: generally between 100 and 150 pieces per style
Lower quantities can be considered, with possible variations linked to production efficiency.

parameter-pricing.v: We believe every company should be able to rely on professional uniforms without compromising its budget. That is why we adapt to your economic needs, offering flexible, customised solutions that guarantee quality, style, and consistency with your brand identity. We work alongside you to find the right balance between investment and result, creating uniforms that strengthen your brand.

parameter-timing.v: Project timelines depend on the complexity of development and the production schedule.
Fully bespoke projects generally require around 8 weeks from initial idea to delivery.
Good planning allows for smoother development and reliable delivery timelines.
